Condamné pour corruption et trafic d'inf: Convicted of corruption and influence peddling (pact with the magistrate Gilbert Azibert). Conviction upheld by the Court of Cassation on 18 December 2024: 3 years in prison, including 1 year without suspension served with an electronic tag, and 3 years of ineligibility.
Financement illégal de la campagne prési: Illegal financing of the 2012 presidential campaign: nearly 43 million euros of spending against a ceiling of 22.5 million, the excess being concealed by a double-invoicing system. Appeal rejected by the Court of Cassation on 26 November 2025: 1 year in prison, including 6 months without suspension, served with an electronic tag.
Condamné en première instance le 25 sept: Sentenced at first instance on 25 September 2025 to 5 years in prison without suspension for criminal conspiracy. Imprisoned on 21 October 2025. Appeal trial from 16 March to 27 May 2026; decision expected on 30 November 2026.
Détournement de fonds du Parlement europ: Misappropriation of European Parliament funds (2004-2016). Convicted at first instance on 31 March 2025, then on appeal on 7 July 2026 to 3 years in prison, 2 of them suspended and 1 year without suspension that can be served under adjustment (electronic tag). Her ineligibility sentence, already served owing to provisional enforcement, leaves her eligible for 2027. She and the other convicts lodged an appeal to the Court of Cassation on 24 July 2026.
Emploi fictif de son épouse comme assist: Fictitious job for his wife as a parliamentary assistant. The Court of Cassation upheld his guilt in 2024 but referred the sentence back to the Paris Court of Appeal, which set it in June 2025: 4 years in prison, suspended, a fine of 375 000 € and 5 years of ineligibility. Sentence final since François Fillon withdrew his appeal in February 2026.
Compte bancaire non déclaré à l'étranger: Undeclared foreign bank account concealed while he was Budget Minister in charge of fighting tax fraud. Convicted on appeal on 15 May 2018 to 4 years in prison, 2 of them suspended, a fine of 300 000 € and 5 years of ineligibility; the part without suspension was served with an electronic tag from 2019.
Dissimulation de patrimoine au fisc par: Concealment of assets from the tax authorities through shell companies. Guilt for aggravated laundering of tax fraud upheld by the Court of Cassation in 2021; sentence set by the Paris Court of Appeal on 9 January 2023: four and a half years in prison, a fine of 100 000 € and 10 years of ineligibility.
Verdict attendu de la cour d'appel dans: Verdict expected from the Court of Appeal in the Libyan financing case (Nicolas Sarkozy)
